 Marty Klinkenberg Published October 21, 2026 Open this photo in gallery: Connor McDavid (centre) is off to a blistering start to the NHL season, with 26 points in nine games. More importantly for the Oilers' captain, his team is 7-1-1 heading into Thursday's game against Carolina. Luke Hales/Getty Images 
 Comments Share Save for later Please log in to bookmark this story. Log In Create an account Even by Connor McDavid’s lofty standards this is the greatest start to a season in his 12-year NHL career. 
 The Edmonton Oilers captain enters Thursday’s contest at Rogers Place against the Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes with 26 points in just nine games. With three assists in Tuesday’s victory over Minnesota he became the fastest player to ever register 20 helpers in a season.
 At his current pace he could reach 100 points before Christmas and shatter the single-season record Wayne Gretzky set in 1985-1986 with 215. McDavid has combined for eight points in his last two outings, has already had two five-point games, one four-point game and two three-pointers. He is yet to be shut out.
 At the same time the Oilers and first-year head coach Mike Babcock are 7-1-1. The last time they started 7-1-1 was 1983-1984 when they sprang out of the gate and won their first of five Stanley Cups in a span of six years.
 McDavid has shrugged off his early accomplishments, which includes already being plus-17.
 Mike Babcock is a lightning rod of attention behind the Oilers’ bench 
 “I think the team is just playing well and when that happens you are going to have success throughout the lineup,” McDavid told reporters this week. “Everybody is playing well, paying attention to details and structure and playing hard. A lot of good things are happening.”
 Edmonton has won all five of its games on the road so far, the best away mark in franchise history. Its game against Carolina is the second in a five-game homestand that continues when the Maple Leafs visit on Saturday, Detroit comes to town on Oct. 26 and Calgary renews acquaintances with its provincial rival on Oct. 28.
 The Oilers’ only loss in regulation time came at the hands of the Utah Mammoth, who entered Wednesday first in the Central Division. The Oilers lost their opener in overtime against Vancouver.
 McDavid is making a mockery of the league right now, but he has had a lot of support. Evan Bouchard leads all NHL defencemen with 18 points and is tied for first with Quinn Hughes with 11 assists.
 Open this photo in gallery: McDavid already has a pair of five-point games this season and is coming off of a win over Minnesota on Tuesday that saw him pick up three assists. Peter Creveling/Reuters 
 Leon Draisaitl has eight goals and 16 points already. Vasily Podkolzin, who plays on the first line with McDavid and Draisaitl, has seven goals. With Freddie Andersen injured, Devon Levi has taken over as the No. 1 goalie and is 5-1.
 “It all starts with Connor,” Zach Hyman, who has been limited to two games due to injury, said. “He is the guy who drives the bus for us. When he plays the way he is playing it makes it easier for everybody else.
 “He’s off to one of the best starts of his career. I think it has a lot to do with our record and where we are but he is obviously the one who is driving it.”
 The Oilers’ top players interviewed Babcock, a veteran coach who has had great success over the course of his career despite some questionable conduct, before he was hired during the off-season.
 The group was led by McDavid, Draisaitl, Hyman and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins. They wanted a tougher more forceful coach after being eliminated by Anaheim in the first round of the playoffs last year. Edmonton lost to the Florida Panthers in the Stanley Cup finals the two seasons that preceded that.
 “Connor has done everything that I have asked and he has done it in such a way that he seems to enjoy it,” Babcock said. “He takes pride in doing things right. It is impossible to coach a team when your best player isn’t driving it and he is driving it. 
 “I just think he is a real good player, but what he is, is a better person and a better man, and he drives his teammates not by what he says but what he what he does. It’s what you model each and every day, and he does it right.”
